utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. From the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes and Mr. Meek. The Prosecution, I recognise the presence of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. That's it. I think there are some preliminaries. Yes, Mr. Thayer? We are all ears.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning, everyone. I was advised by my friend Mr. Zivanovic this morning that there was a tendering issue with respect to an item that came in through -- or that was tendered through a prior witness the Exhibit number's P0295, it is a working vehicle log. Two pages had originally been tendered by the Nikolic team, I believe, in connection with the testimony of PW 101. Two separate pages were tendered by the Popovic team more recently and Mr. Nicholls tendered a couple of pages through his witness. The document is 604 pages long. Tendering bits and pieces I understand has created some difficulty with our friends in the Registry. What I would propose is that we mark for identification the entire 600 page document, which has been translated in full already, which I think makes all the difference in the world for everyone. We may continue to refer to it and refer to particular pages but given the fact that it's translated I don't anticipate any objections from my friends. I would suggest we tender it in its entirety at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the position of the Defence teams on this? Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Bourgon? You are the two who have made use of it. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we used two pages of this document, Your Honour, and we would like to tender these two pages, we sent a list about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But do you oppose the Prosecution suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So as I understand it, we had two pages introduced already by you, Mr. Bourgon, or by your team?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I believe there were more than two pages but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: More than two pages, all right. So there are two pages which are now being sought to be tendered by Mr. Zivanovic. Those would be admitted. But the whole document will be marked for identification for the time being, and then we'll see what we need. The suggestion is to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I misspoke. I would suggest that we just admit the whole document in its entirety since it's been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That makes more sense because in actual fact my reaction was going to be while you were talking, first, whether there is a translation issue which obviously there isn't, and secondly, whether there is a need for to have a 600-page document admitted if there are only a few pages that you are relying upon. So it did make sense for some time to have it marked for identification and then the relative pages, but if there is consensus on having the whole document admitted straight away on the assumption that it's going to be made use of further, later on, then I think that's the best way to go about it. Agreed, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we agree also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are four pages, those are travel orders, we have already agreed to several of them. I don't think there is any reason at this moment not to accept them, not to admit them as one document because they all have their numbers. And the Prosecution will certainly use all the pages, and they can be admitted as an exhibit. I do not share therefore the view of my colleagues and take a separate position.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The number of pages is 604.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may be mistaken but I think the documents to which my friend is referring to is a separate group of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is another group of documents. I mean, I didn't want to say that. I thought he would bring it out yourself. So we have no problems with this document. It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: While I'm standing on this general topic, Mr. President, we are close to completing the complete translation of the duty officer notebook. I think the aim from our team translator was to have it completed by tomorrow. I think she's on schedule. I will let my friends know as soon as it's completed. But we are close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's nice music to our ears and I think also to Mr. Sarapa and Mr. Haynes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little mistake in line 3 on page 3, line 15. It says four pages but it's actually 604.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it was corrected in lines 22 and 23. Yes. Anything else? Any preliminary matters? None. So let's bring in the next witness -- yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe this witness could use a caution from the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And he has -- there are no protective measures to my knowledge, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence. And before doing so, you're required to make a solemn declaration that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth. Madam Usher is going to hand you the text of the solemn declaration. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. Take a seat. Mr. Thayer is about to start firing his questions at you. He will then be followed by the various Defence teams on cross-examination. But before you start giving evidence, I've been asked to alert you to a right that you enjoy under our rules, namely the right not to be forced to incriminate yourself. This is a right that you enjoy, as I said, but it is not an absolute right so I need to explain to you what the position is. It's not to be excluded that you could be asked questions which, if you answer, could tend to incriminate you. I'm not saying that this will be the case but it could be the case. In such a case, you have a right to stop before giving your answer and ask the Trial Chamber to exempt you from answering such incriminatory questions. We will hear what you have to say and then we will decide whether to exempt you from answering such questions or whether to compel you to answer such a question. If we exempt you, then obviously you don't answer that question. If we compel you to answer that question, then you need to answer that question truthfully pursuant to the oath, to the solemn undertaking that you've taken today. If you are so compelled, however, you enjoy a further right under our rules, namely that whatever you state in answering such incriminatory questions will not be made use of as evidence against you in any subsequent proceedings, except if the proceedings arise out of you giving false testimony. Is that -- have I explained it clear enough to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were you made aware of such right before you came into this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can safely proceed. Mr. Thayer, he's in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Predrag Celic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How old are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: 33, going on 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where were you born and raised?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I was born in Sekovici and grew up in a place called Jakovica, next door to Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you identify yourself as a Bosnian Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, how you're currently employed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I'm a member of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. I work in the public security centre of Bijeljina in a support unit located in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what kind of work do you do in that unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We provide security escort, we do arrests, we provide security at football matches, and other work which does not fall within regular police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long have you been doing that job, approximately?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Since 2000 I've been in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to that, how were you employed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Before that, I was a member of the Special Police Brigade, the 2nd Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we'll talk about that detachment in a moment, sir. What I want to do right now is briefly review with you your service history during the war and I'll just summarise it very briefly, if I could. Just correct anything I may get wrong. After completing your military service, you served as a member of the Intervention Platoon in the Sekovici Brigade which was headquartered in Trnovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And May 12th of 1993 you joined the 2nd Sekovici Detachment of the Special Police Brigade which you just referred to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where was the 2nd Sekovici Detachment headquartered?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Detachment of Sekovici was based in the hotel in Sekovici. The name of the hotel is Lovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just generally, sir, where is Sekovici geographically located in relation to the Srebrenica opstina, north, south, east or west?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I can't tell exactly. I think -- I think west.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. In July of 1995, who commanded the 2nd Sekovici Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, the commander of the detachment was Rade Cuturic, nicknamed Oficir, Officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm looking at my transcript, sir, and it looks like it didn't pick up the last name of this individual named Oficir, could you repeat his last name, please?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Rade Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It also looks like it didn't pick up the nickname. What was Mr. Cuturic's nickname?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Oficir -- O-f-i-c-i-r.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Cuturic's actual position in the detachment, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, he was commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you a slightly different question. Prior to Mr. Cuturic taking command of the detachment in about July of 1995, who was in command of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Before Rade Cuturic, there was Miso Stupar as commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know approximately when Mr. Cuturic took over from Mr. Stupar as commander?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I think it was in June, when we were sent out into the field to Sarajevo, Rade Cuturic accompanied us on that mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when Mr. Stupar was the commander of your detachment, what was Mr. Cuturic's position when Mr. Stupar was in command?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: He was the deputy, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you suppose, sir, or do you know from your experience and recollection that that was in fact the case?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: That was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in June of 1995, when Mr. Stupar was in command of your detachment, who was his immediate superior commander?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The immediate superior was the commander of the brigade of the Special Police, Goran Saric, and his deputy Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In July of 1995, sir, approximately how many infantry soldiers did the Sekovici Detachment have? And I mean active.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: There were three platoons of infantry. The 1st, the 2nd and the 3rd platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: And there was also a logistics platoon on top of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, in total, how many infantry soldiers did those three platoons add up to, just approximately, if you can give the Court an idea?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Infantry? In July?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Three platoons, adding up to around 40 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall who the commander of the 1st Platoon was in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe it was Marko Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about the 2nd Platoon, sir? In July of 1995, who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Platoon in July 1995 -- how shall I put it? We were in Sarajevo, in the field, and the commander, Velimir Kitaljevic was wounded there, before the arrival in the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that the 2nd Platoon did not have an actual commander?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what platoon were you in, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 3rd Sekovici Platoon?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Platoon, which hailed from Skelani, was Milenko Trifunovic, also known as Cop.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was that 3rd platoon also known as the Skelani platoon, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, given that your 2nd Platoon leader had been injured, from whom would your platoon typically receive its orders in June and July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From the detachment commander, Rade Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about the types of equipment and uniforms that you wore in your detachment. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what types of mechanised weaponry your detachment had?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We had a Praga, two tanks, and we also had a three-barrelled piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the model of the tank? Do you know the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the three-barrelled piece, is that also known as a BOV or a B-O-V?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: That was an armoured vehicle, a BOV, a three-barrelled piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And would this mechanised weaponry typically accompany your detachment when it was deployed on an operation, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation. Sometimes they would, sometimes they wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you also have mortar support?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you personally, sir, were you issued any type of weapon in particular?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I had an M-84 machine-gun. This is what I was issued with in the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what type of rifle was the average member of your detachment issued, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you carry hand grenades, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Some did, some didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about you personally? Was that a part of your standard equipment?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: One, two perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the uniform that your detachment wore, for the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you please describe the uniform that your detachment wore? What did it look like? What did it consist of? Colour?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We had camouflage overalls. There were also two-piece uniforms. As far as I can remember, on the left shoulder we had a patch featuring the words "Special Brigade" and beneath it, "The police" and the patch featured a number and in the middle, there was a flag with the coat of arms featuring a two-headed eagle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during the war, sir, what was the general nature of your detachment's assignments?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: During the war, we were mostly engaged in combat assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you were a police detachment but in terms of your command structure and operation, was it civilian or military in nature?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We were attached to the Special Brigade of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, can you describe in general how orders were communicated down the chain of command in your organisation?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, within your Special Police Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was the brigade commander who issued orders. Next down in the chain was the deputy, and then the order would travel down to the detachment commanders. As far as I know, or at least that's how things should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in your experience, was that how the Special Police Brigade operated, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to July, specifically, of 1995. Actually, let me back up. I want to focus your attention first on June, and into July. Where was your platoon deployed in June of 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: In June 1995, as I've already told you, we were in Sarajevo, near the so-called Srednji part of the Sarajevo theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what were you doing there, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: There, we were trying to regain a defence line that had fallen near the settlement of Srednji.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you ordered to pull out of that area for some reason?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We were told to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were told to withdraw, what the date was?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was in the evening, on the 11th, around 8.00 or 9.00 in the evening. I can't exactly -- it was between 7.00 and 9.00 in the evening anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, sir, this is the 11th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So where did you go, sir, from Srednji?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We arrived in the area of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether that area had a particular name? And can you describe where it was approximately in relation to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We arrived in a school in Bjelovac. This is where we were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall who informed your platoon that it was going to be pulled back and redeployed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The entire unit was pulled out. It was the detachment commander who issued that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you arrived and then settled in in Bjelovac, do you recall whether your 2nd Platoon only was there or were you joined by the other two Sekovici platoons on the night of the 11th?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We were all there, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether any other Special Police Brigade detachments arrived at that location in Bjelovac? For example, specific detachments or elements from the Jahorina training centre? Do you know whether any of those forces also arrived in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: As for the Special Police, I don't know whether anybody from the brigade was there, in addition to us. But there were some other people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "other people", sir, are you referring to MUP forces or some other forces or can you not recall?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. I want to turn your attention to the morning of 12 July, sir. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: In the morning of the 12th of July, maybe around 8.00 or 9.00 in the morning, we set out from Bratunac in the direction of Srebrenica. We arrived at the Yellow Bridge where the road forks off towards the right. This is where we turned right towards a place which I believe is called Budak. That's where we were deployed and stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's an issue of translation, I believe. Here on page 15, line 4, it says, "We arrived at the Yellow Bridge where the road forks off toward the right." The witness I believe said something else. He didn't say that the road forks to the right but he said we forked to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you followed that, Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you agree with what Mr. Lazarevic has just corrected in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We turned right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I thank my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to resume your narrative. Before that, though, how did you arrive? How were you transported to this location? What types of vehicle or vehicles did you take?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Most of us were transported by a Dubrava bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that bus, sir, was that a detachment bus, an official detachment vehicle?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you arrive at this position, you turned right towards a place that you recalled being called Budak. What did you do when you arrived at this position, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: This is where we were deployed in a line, and if needed, we were supposed to scour the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall who communicated that assignment to your platoon?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We were told by the commander before we left where we were going, why we were going there, and what our mission was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you given any instructions as to what to do if you encountered anybody while you were deployed there?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: In case we encountered a civilian, we would have to keep that person, we would have to call our superior officers, and what they would do, I don't know. I'm talking about civilians here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about if the person was not or did not appear to be a civilian, sir? Were your instructions any different?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: If any such person had weapons and opened fire at us, then we would open fire in return.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Understood. Now, if an armed person surrendered, were your instructions any different than what they were with respect to the civilians?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The same. That person would have been handed over to our superior and with that, my part of the job would end.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You testified that you established a line in case you had to conduct a search. Did you, in fact, have to conduct such a search, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At your position, do you recall seeing any other police or army units there where you were?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from your position, sir, what if anything could you see of the village of Potocari or the UN base?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From that place, one could see things down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did you see, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I could see that there were a lot of people there, and some facilities as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see both civilians and people who appeared to you to be soldiers, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that I saw people, but this was not close enough for me to tell exactly who they were. There may have been men in uniform among them, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you move from your position that morning, other than leaving eventually?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We left that position and went down to the road. After a certain while we withdrew from that area and we arrived in the direction of Bratunac and from there, we went towards Konjevic Polje. We went in the direction of Konjevic Polje, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And before we get to that next stage, sir, I just want to ask you a couple of questions about the time you were near Potocari. Did you actually come across anyone while you were at your position in Budak?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: While I was on position, I did not come across anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And approximately how long or how many hours do you recall being in that position?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Maybe an hour or two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You just indicated that you were travelling in the direction of Konjevic Polje and would that have been on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the vicinity of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of the day this was, when you stopped?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did when you stopped in the area of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know when, but after a certain time we were deployed on that road from Sandici towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your assignment at that point?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The assignment was to secure the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, and to protect the villages that were around it, Kravica and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, secure and protect from whom or from what in particular?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From the people who were moving through the forest. These people had left the area of Srebrenica or were leaving the area of Srebrenica, and as it turned out later on, they were headed for Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate approximately what length of this road your platoon was responsible for securing?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: You mean the detachment?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, actually I specifically mean your platoon. Can you estimate what length of the road your platoon was responsible for securing?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, since we were relatively few, we didn't cover a great length.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And whatever that length was on the road, sir, where you and your platoon were deployed, can you describe where that section of the road was in relation to Kravica and Sandici?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I didn't quite understand it. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure. The location where you and your platoon were deployed, was it closer to Kravica or was it closer to Sandici?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Perhaps closer to Sandici. It was closer to Sandici than to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who ordered you and your platoon to deploy along that particular portion of the road?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was the order of the detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, as you head --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: As we deployed from Sandici on, and we stopped at certain points and deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as you head in the direction of Konjevic Polje from your location, which platoon was closest to yours, as you were heading towards Sandici and Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The 1st Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know where the 3rd Platoon was deployed, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, physically, how were you and your fellow platoon members deployed along your section of that road?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We were deployed in groups of two or three men so that we can see each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there any type of feature or structure where you were positioned, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: There was one house at the point where I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the distance approximately of that house to the road?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: 40 to 50 metres to the left on the side of the road, if you are looking from Kravica towards Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of your 2nd Platoon colleagues who were near your position?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: You mean the men who were with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: At that house, Brano Dzinic was with me, Zoran Tomic, nicknamed Zgembo, and Slobodan Stjepanovic, nicknamed Sule.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall the names of any of your other colleagues who may have been on your left or your right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: On my left there were Milenko Pepic and Ljubisa Becarevic. And also Mile Bojanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you aware of any other police or VRS forces being deployed along the road, not necessarily at your position but in the area of Kravica through Sandici and along that portion towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall specifically any units by name that were deployed there, other than your detachment?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I know that in the area from Sandici towards Konjevic Polje, there was the 1st Company of the police. I don't know about other units. I don't know which units they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, going in the other direction, sir, towards Bratunac, did you ever see the structure that is sometimes referred to as the agricultural hangar or warehouse at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I hadn't passed through before, so when we arrived I saw that structure and after a while I found out it was an agricultural cooperative located to the left of the road, if you're going from Bratunac towards Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate approximately how far that warehouse was from your location in the house where you were positioned?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Around 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know which units, if any, were deployed in front of that facility?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which 2nd Sekovici Detachment platoon was deployed closest to that warehouse, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I described the location where I was. The men from my platoon who were to the left of me were next, the 1st Platoon was to the right. I really don't know where the Skelani platoon was. But then the 2nd Platoon must have been the closest to my location, and those colleagues from the same platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you spend the night of 12 July in that house, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That brings us to the 13th. Did you receive any information on the 13th of any incidents that occurred during the night of the 12th along that road between Kravica and Sandici?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I heard, I don't know from whom, that one member of the 1st Company of the police had gotten killed up there near Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you hear how that police officer had been killed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, rumour had it that a grenade had been thrown and the man got killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, it's a translation issue. It's on page 22, line 2, the answer of the witness as it is recorded here says, "But then the 2nd Platoon must have been the closest to my location" and if I remember correctly, the witness said, it was closest to the location of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you agree to that, Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I thank my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you referred to the 1st Company of the police, and forgive me if I asked you this before, I just can't recall, that 1st Company was attached to what unit or entity, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The 1st Police Company belonged to the then-public security centre of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you remain in your position at that house during the day on the 13th, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did any of your commanders come by that day to check on your positions and deployment?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, the detachment commander passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during these two days, the 12th and the 13th, did he do that more than once?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Several times, I suppose, as long as we were there in that area, and he toured that terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was he doing as he was touring the terrain?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: He kept an eye on where we were, he warned us to take cover so that nobody would be killed, things like that. He told us to hold on and that we would be withdrawing soon because we had already been in the field around Sarajevo or in Sarajevo for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what kind of communication equipment was Mr. Cuturic and other commanders using during this time, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Motorolas, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall who was issued those Motorolas, who was using them?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The detachment commander, platoon commanders, the men on combat vehicles and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during these two days, sir, to the best of your recollection, from whom was Mr. Cuturic receiving his orders?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose Mr. Cuturic received orders from his superior, Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether or not you saw Mr. Borovcanin in that area on the 12th or the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him. He might have been there. He might have passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And given your experience, sir, in the field as a Special Police Brigade member, would you have expected Mr. Borovcanin to be in that area as Mr. Cuturic was?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I object to this question. I mean he's here to testify on his actual knowledge what happened there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. What's your response to that, Mr. Thayer? Do you wish to proceed with your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I will take the Court's suggestion and move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what kind of vehicle traffic did you observe along the road on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Buses passed by, trucks, other vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the buses and the trucks, who or what did they contain, from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Civilians from the area of Srebrenica, Potocari, from up there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you saw similar traffic the day before, on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I think in the afternoon there was traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On the 12th or the 13th, do you recall any attempts by Serb forces to communicate with the people who were in the woods?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Could you clarify what you mean by "communicate"?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, from your position, did you hear anything being said that was loud enough for you to hear, from your position?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: A megaphone was audible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what do you recall being said through the megaphone?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was not quite clearly audible but it could be understood. The people from the forest were called upon to come out on to the road and surrender, that nobody would touch them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in what direction did you hear this calling out on the microphone coming from?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It came from the direction of Sandici, to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from your position at that house, looking in the direction of Sandici and Konjevic Polje, were you able to see some of the hills and the clearings in that direction from where you were?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From my vantage point I could see in front of me a meadow and the forest. And to the right, as the land lies, there were some clearings and then came a slope towards Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you able to see anybody moving about in that area that you described, that slope up near Sandici?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Occasionally people passed by, in those clearings where there was no trees, they descended towards the brook, but I couldn't see further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate approximately how far from your house this area that you were just talking about was?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The forest where they descended?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps 800 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did any Muslim men surrender at your location on the 12th or the 13th?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Nobody surrendered where I stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, other than the buses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BEARA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I really have to leave the room for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please the security officers, I don't know how the arrangement is --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Perhaps we could take the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we can take the break now. It's in five minutes' time anyway, so -- 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President for accommodating us earlier before the break. I just want to let you know we appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can take it for granted that that will always be the case. We try to keep a watchful eye all the time but we are watching the Prosecution, watching the witness, we are watching you, we are following the transcript and putting our -- inserting our notes, et cetera, so sometimes you might be looking at the other side of what is really happening. So you will understand that too. But I noticed Colonel Beara straight away. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, other than the buses and trucks filled with civilians that you mentioned previously, did you see any prisoners on the 13th along that road?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: On the 13th, sometime in the afternoon, quite a large group of prisoners was moving from the direction of Sandici towards Kravica. I couldn't put a number, maybe 600, 800 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how were they moving? Were they on foot or were they in vehicles?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: They were walking in a column, on one part of the road, one lane.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this column being escorted by anyone, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could not recognise the escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell this Trial Chamber whether those escorts were MUP or whether they were VRS?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I didn't notice any members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you have any prior knowledge or information that this column was going to be passing by your position?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I was not informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What could you observe about the people in the column? Were they men and women, just men only? How were they dressed? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I didn't really pay attention because there was shooting coming from the forest, but as far as I was able to see, they were in civilian clothes, there were some in uniform, and they were walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, were these men and women or men only, from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From what I was able to see, they were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from what you were able to see, were any of those men armed, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At the time, did you know where those prisoners were being taken?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, after some time, I don't know exactly how much time, I heard shooting coming from down there to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say, "Down there to my left," do you mean in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you described -- you referred to some shooting you heard coming from the forest. Can you please describe the shooting that you're talking about now that was coming from the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The shooting from the direction of Kravica was quite louder, and lasted for longer intervals. I wouldn't be able to give you the interval times and durations.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How did this shooting that you heard coming from the direction of Kravica differ from this shooting that you were hearing from the woods and throughout your deployment in this area?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was much louder and stronger.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything else coming from the direction of Kravica, after you heard this stronger, louder shooting?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I could also hear detonations resounding. I believe that bombs were being thrown.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you say "bombs" sir or it's being translated as "bombs", what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Based upon what you were hearing, sir, did you form any impression to yourself as to what was happening down that road in the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I believe that there had been a conflict there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, at the time that you were hearing this, you had just seen, you said, 600 to 800 unarmed prisoners being led in the direction of Kravica. When you use the term "conflict," please tell the Trial Chamber, as you were sitting there listening to this shooting and explosions, what you thought was happening down that road to those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you're being asked by the interpreter to repeat your answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I thought that the civilians were being shot at, that fire was opened on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you communicate with any of your colleagues about what you were hearing?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: The person who was with me, we were talking, we were making assumptions as to what might have been going on and how this conflict or, how shall I put it, might have occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, what happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: What do you mean what happened next?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did you do next after you heard what was going on down the road?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I remained in my position. I did not leave my area of responsibility, up to the evening when we finally withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how were you advised or ordered to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Who issued the order, it was either Rado Cuturic or one of the platoon commanders, I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where did you withdraw to and how were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we withdrew in the direction of Konjevic Polje on the bus that I have already mentioned, the 1st and the 2nd Platoon. The 3rd Skelani Platoon, I'm not sure about that unit. It is possible that they withdrew in the direction of Skelani. Later on, I heard a story that a member of the detachment from Skelani had gotten killed in that area where all these civilians were killed, and that one of the officers was wounded, that his arm was burned. So it is quite possible that they were not taken to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about this story that you heard about the events at the Kravica warehouse. First of all, do you recall whether or not you heard this account while you were in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where were you physically positioned or staying while you were in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, we were in Konjevic Polje, we were at the crossroads of the Zvornik-Bratunac-Kravica road. We were on the right-hand side from the direction of Bratunac, very close to the crossroads. We were in the houses nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to this account of the events in the warehouse. You indicated that you heard that a member of the Skelani Platoon had been killed there. Do you recall what that member of the Skelani Platoon's name was?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Krsto Dragicevic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did he have a nickname, sir, that you knew?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Krle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in this account that you heard, how was Mr. Dragicevic killed?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From what I heard, one person, somebody among the prisoners, snatched the rifle from the deceased and killed him. And then he also tried to kill the officer. However, the officer grabbed the rifle barrel and he was holding on to that barrel while the bullet was being fired from the rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's basically a matter of translation but when saying "officer", I believe that we already used the nickname Oficir and he was referring to the person with the nickname Oficir, and here it said tried to kill the officer. So it could be understood in multiple ways so -- to make sure that it's clear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very valid point. Perhaps you can clear it up with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I was going to let him finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you refer to "the officer", sir, and I think you heard the comment from my friend and I thank him, who were you referring to when you referred to somebody grabbing the rifle and being injured, just so the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Rado Cuturic, also known as Oficir or Officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And according to this account that you heard, what injuries, if any, did Mr. Cuturic sustain as a result of grabbing the barrel of the gun?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Burns.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this may sound like an obvious question but do you know where Mr. Dragicevic was from?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about the rest of the members of his platoon? Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: They were billeted in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, were most of them from the Skelani area to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's this 3rd Skelani Platoon, sir, to which Mr. Dragicevic belonged that you were telling the Trial Chamber you don't remember where they were located along the road on the 12th and the 13th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during these two days on the 12th and the 13th, do you recall whether the detachment's tanks or its Praga or the three-barrelled BOV were with your detachment there in the field?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: There were combat vehicles but I don't know whether they were ours or somebody else's.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, which or what kind of combat vehicles do you recall being there in that area?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I spotted a tank in Sandici. I don't know whether I saw a Praga or a BOV. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing a Praga or a BOV being fired during the 12th and the 13th in the area of that road, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I could hear sporadic shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention now to the next day, the 14th of July. Did you leave Konjevic Polje and, if so, where were you deployed next?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: We left Konjevic Polje and we went in the direction of Zvornik, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your next assignment, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Because of the large concentration of the then-Muslims and currently Bosniaks, who were moving towards Zvornik and further on towards Tuzla, we had to go to Baljkovica to protect the Serbian villages around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what if anything happened in that area of Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: In the area of Baljkovica, there was fierce fighting going on on the 16th, between members of the BiH army, on the one hand, and members of the VRS and members of the Ministry of the Interior, on the other. This is a rather small area where a lot of troops were concentrated on both sides, on theirs as well as ours. At the same time, the BiH army was attacking our positions from the direction of Tuzla. This is where I was wounded, and I had to be pulled out from the area and taken to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately -- or do you remember the date on which you were wounded, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: It was on the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did the Serb forces at Baljkovica suffer killed and wounded as a result of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you were wounded, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I was taken to the hospital in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the scene at the hospital in Zvornik when you were there for your treatment? What was happening?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived at the hospital, I had been wounded in the right thigh, and the doctors did not consider me an urgent case. That's why I was sitting in the corridor and waiting, whereas other patients who had been brought from the front line, who had been more seriously wounded, would be treated immediately. And then at one point, I fainted as a result of the loss of blood, and then I was treated. The staff was in a state of alert. They were quite on the edge because of the number of wounded that were being brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, sir, were members of the VRS and MUP killed during this action in Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know. In my estimate, 30 or so people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to show you a document that we went through together yesterday. This is P01891. And I think to save some time what I would like to do with Madam Usher's assistance is simply to show this original to the witness, ask him to flip through it rather than asking for the B/C/S on e-court. This is a logbook from the Zvornik hospital. There are portions of it that are under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to point out that to you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I will not be asking the witness to identify any specific patient information other than that which may pertain to himself. What I'd like to do is if we could perhaps also use the ELMO when we get to particular pages. For those who are following in English, I will be turning the witness's attention to pages 22 through 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I just ask you to turn to the first yellow-tabbed page and just ask you if a see a date next to the entry 4606 of this logbook, and perhaps if we could place it under the ELMO, just to throw it up there quickly?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What is the date there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could just quickly display that on the ELMO. This is ERN 0118-0285.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have an English page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that should be page 22 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The English translation is, we've had this problem before, pretty poor because of the illegibility of some of the writing so I'm afraid it's not going to be particularly helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you would turn to the next yellow-tabbed page in that document, do you see a date on the entry 4671? This is page 25 of the English translation?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, what is that date there?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd ask you to flip one, two, three, four, five pages, I think, to the next tabbed page. Do you see an entry at 4721?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see a name there, sir, and a year of birth?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Predrag Celic, 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that the year of your birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is page 29 of the English translation. Lastly, sir, if you would turn to the final tabbed page, do you see an entry at 47 -- or a date at 4749, partially in Roman numerals? This is page 31 of the English. What is the date there, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Should I take this?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you can -- sure and if you could just read the date there in that entry that's 4749.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Here at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Do you see the date that's right there at that entry?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: 4/17 Roman numeral III, and then there is 95 or what's that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think we have a legibility problem, sir. Could that be a Roman numeral VII that's in that entry there following the 17?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Possible. There is a line here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. I think we're done with this exhibit. Now, sir, we were a little short on time yesterday. I want to show you a photograph we didn't have a chance to look at but I think you've looked at this before. I'm going to ask you if you recognise anybody in the photograph. For the record this is ERN 0216-4738, chapter 18, page 3, of P01936. It's also a video still from the trial video P02047. Do you recognise anyone in this photograph, sir? Do you see an image in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I do. I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who do you see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I see two persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise either of those two people, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, the interpreters didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of those two people, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I know the person who is to my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that the individual with the ammunition across his chest, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: His name is Mirko and his nickname is Dugi.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how do you know him, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: He was also a member of the Skelani detachment -- the Skelani Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recognise the person next to him, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this individual that you've identified as Dugi is still living?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: From what I heard, he died after the war, got killed after the war. I think he was working with electricity somewhere and he got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of seeing this individual named Dugi along the road where you were deployed on the 12th or the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember, maybe I saw him, maybe I didn't. I couldn't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about Mr. Cuturic, sir, Oficir? Do you know whether he is still living?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: He is no longer alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to show you another picture, sir. This is from a video clip that we reviewed together yesterday, also it's a video still that you also saw with me yesterday. I'm just going to ask you if you recognise the individual in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one are you referring him to? The one in the foreground?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone in this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I know the person with the bandanna.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's the person in the foreground with the white bandanna, sir? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Who is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: That's Milenko Trifunovic, nicknamed Cop.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: For the record this is ERN 0216-4735, chapter 18, page 2 of P01936, video still taken from P02047. Sir, how is it that you are familiar or acquainted with Cop?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I know Cop. He was the commander of the Skelani Platoon, and Skelani was -- he used to come to the Sekovici base as required when he needed to pick up food for that platoon or something else. He used to come rather often. They sometimes went to the Sekovici base as well. So I know him rather well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did any superior officer in the Special Police Brigade ever ask you for a report concerning the actions of you or your platoon in Potocari or along the road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Other than statements you may have provided to Defence counsel in the ongoing case in Sarajevo, other than your testimony in that court, other than our first meeting a couple of days ago, has anyone ever asked you to submit a report about your actions or your platoon's actions in Potocari or along that Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't think I understand quite. Could you make the question clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll do my best, sir. Other than any statements or testimony you may have given in connection with the case in Sarajevo, and other than meeting with me for the first time a couple of days ago, has anyone else asked you to provide a report or an account of your activities, your platoon's activities, in Potocari or along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I think that I gave a statement to what's his name, the counsel of Brano Dzinic, Suzana something.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Ms. Tomanovic, but that was in connection with the case in Sarajevo, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Other than that, to the best of your recollection, no one has ever asked to you file a report about your activities in Potocari and along the road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Lazarevic, I suppose you would wish to go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure you wanted to go first. In the meantime in order to more or less assess how much time you can have, for the record, the Gvero and Pandurevic team do not wish to cross-examine this witness, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Nikolic team? One moment, one moment, Ms. Nikolic. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in view of the examination-in-chief, we decided to ask three questions. That will take no longer than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Nikolic team?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We'll have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the evidence given by this witness so far, we decided not to ask any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We'll not cross-examine this witness also, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no questions at this time. We reserve the right in case we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, that doesn't entitle you to go on beyond what you had in mind, Mr. Stojanovic, but I think you have got more than the hour that you asked for. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think we'll be done before the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Celic, I appear here with my colleagues for Mr. Borovcanin, and I have a couple of questions for you regarding these events. You said today that at this moment you are a member of a support unit that is part of the MUP of Republika Srpska and that is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose in order to do that job, you had to be vetted and certified for that job in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as everyone else?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who does the vetting? Are there any international representatives involved?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Practically, you've been a member of the Sekovici unit from 1993?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, you were barely 20 when you joined the Sekovici unit?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke today about the composition of that unit and you mentioned one platoon that you called the Skelani Platoon.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I want to ask you about that platoon. How far is Skelani from Sekovici, where the base of your platoon was?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact distance, but around 100 kilometres or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that in order to reach Skelani, one had to pass through the territory of Serbia, because there were the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica standing in the way between you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We crossed through the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, how many approximately were in that Skelani Platoon?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but detachments had 20 to 25 men. Whether all of them were in the field deployed, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your evidence that in the evening or the night on the 11th of July, between 1900 and 2100 hours, you departed from the Sarajevo theatre of war towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after this answer, let me note that on page 25 -- sorry, page 43, lines 25 and page 44, line 1, the answer of the witness was misstated regarding the number of men in a unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Maybe it was a slip on the part of the witness but the witness did say "detachment".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So can you clarify your point? Because although I have understood what the interpreter said, I'm not sure that I have understood you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly what I see in the record, the answer of the witness is recorded as follows: A detachment had 20 to 25 men, whereas the answer actually had to do with the number of men in a platoon, as part of a detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's clear this up. We are told, Mr. Celic, that you did mention -- use the word "detachment" but the question you need to answer is how many approximately were in the platoon, in the Skelani Platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A platoon had 20 to 25 members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That is clear enough for you now, Mr. Stojanovic? Okay. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Celic. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The next thing I want to ask you, to the best of your recollection, when did you arrive at that school-house in the Bjelovac village near Bratunac, bearing in mind your time of departure from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time but perhaps around midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That night of the 11th, after midnight, you spent the night at the school, right?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that from the Sarajevo theatre of war, you were pulled out precisely at the time of intensive fighting and attacks coming from the 1st Corps of the BH army on the positions of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG CELIC
